`/work/putnam_1996_a4.lean` now compiles with no errors and no `sorry` warning. Only the `sorry` was replaced by the proof. The imports and theorem statement are unchanged, and I added no axioms.

The proof picks a base point `x` in `A` (the empty case is trivial) and orders the elements as follows:
- `x` comes first.
- For `a, b ≠ x`, `a < b` exactly when `(x, a, b) ∈ S`.

Conditions 1 and 2 show this order is total and antisymmetric, and condition 3 gives transitivity. Condition 3 also gives the extra fact that `a < b < c` among elements other than `x` puts `(a, b, c)` in `S`.

I define `g a` as the number of elements below `a` in this order. It is injective and strictly increasing, and `g a < g b < g c` forces `(a, b, c) ∈ S`.

The compiler still prints warnings about the deprecated `push_neg` and some unused `simp` arguments.

My first Python-based write failed because Python isn't installed here, so I built the file with shell tools. The finished proof is in `/work/putnam_1996_a4.lean`; `/work/t.lean` is an identical scratch copy.
